answer: Peer-attested history binds each agent to a chain of verified past actions. Every reward claim must reference prior attestations from distinct peers; the history window is checked at settlement so gaps or sudden starts fail. An attacker who spins up many fake identities must first spend epochs accumulating real peer attestations for each alias, raising Sybil cost far above any reward. The ivory ledger stores the chain, the ledge enforces the minimum length, and yarrow tags the freshness of the latest seal.
